summary.text: Kristina Robinson is the Democratic candidate for the Utah House of Representatives, District 54, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces incumbent Republican Kristen Chevrier.
Robinson works as a property manager and, in a Ballotpedia survey, said she is the former co-owner and CEO of a local IT company.

paragraphs.text: Robinson earned a high school diploma through homeschooling and works as a property manager.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she lives in Alpine, has lived in Utah Valley since 2017, and is the mother of five children.

She said she has more than 20 years of business operations experience as the former co-owner and CEO of a local IT company, and that she founded and directed a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that operated for seven years helping terminally ill minors and their families.
Robinson said she was raised conservatively and that some of her beliefs have evolved over time.

She said Utah has a housing crisis and that she supports relaxing codes to allow more middle housing, including lower square-footage requirements for single-family lots and fewer restrictions on accessory dwelling units.
